method.blender: the travel estimator chain on the Blender dump of the clip at the dump's sample rate (method_a, else method_a_run2; blender.estimator) with the clip's cyclic flag; rel_diff only when both sides used the same estimator; gt_max_mm / gt_max_t = worst heel/ball distance to the dump over its samples and its time; profile_diff_m = largest distance between body_profile's displacement and the contact path run on the dump's frames (same sample times), profile_peak_speed = that dump profile's peak speed (null without a body_profile)
method.body_profile: non-cyclic leg clips, at the clip's sample times t_k (the contact path): per step t_k -> t_k+1 every heel/ball point whose height stays within 0.06 m of its lowest height in the clip is a contact candidate with body velocity u = -(its horizontal displacement) / step and cost (height / 0.02 m)^2 + (vertical speed / 0.3 m/s)^2; a path takes at most one candidate per step and costs the candidate costs + 12 per step without one + the summed squared body acceleration in units of 6.0 m/s^2 (a linear velocity ramp between candidates up to 0.5 s apart, held before the first / after the last); each step's velocity is its mean over all paths weighted exp(-cost / 2) (forward-backward). Body displacement fwd (+Z) / side (+X = left) is the cumulative sum from 0 at t = 0; speed[k] = |displacement| central difference (one-sided at the ends); coverage = expected fraction of steps whose velocity comes from a candidate. The continuity term rejects a swing foot that skims the ground or a heel still descending (which an.py method B, the lowest point per step, integrates as body travel) and keeps a push-off foot on its toes
method.chest_height: skeleton-space y of spined in the aim-idle base clip at t = 0; stand/crouch = mean over weapons
method.cyclic: travel.cyclic (and the wrap of travel / plant / contact estimates) = the loop flag the graph export gives the clip: any dict in actor_b_graph.json with a string `clip` and a boolean `loop` (roles, aim_move, aim_trees, actions, runtime_roles, ...), looped if any entry loops (cyclic_source graph_loop); clips no entry plays and the built-in list use the feet seam test, every heel/ball's first and last samples within 0.02 m horizontally (cyclic_source feet_seam). travel.seam_m = that largest horizontal mismatch; loop / loop_err stay the measured core-bone seam
method.fidelity: clips.*.fidelity_warning lists why a dumped clip's library values are not the authored ones: |blender.rel_diff| > 0.05 or travel heading > 10 deg off blender.heading_deg (both speeds >= 0.1 m/s), blender.gt_max_mm > 20 (at gt_max_t), blender.profile_diff_m > 0.05 m; null otherwise and without the dump. The library (Actor_B.res) is key-reduced; a dropped key shows up here
method.gt_check: every dump3.jsonl clip in the library: Godot heel/ball skeleton-space positions vs Blender (x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y) at t = k / sample_rate
method.loop: first vs last sample of the core bones (chains root..l_ball/r_ball/heada/l_wrist/r_wrist; all keyed bones when none is keyed): skeleton-space position <= 0.02 m and local rotation <= 0.05 rad; 1-sample pose clips are loops; loop_err holds the worst values. Measured only: whether a role loops at runtime comes from actor_b_graph.json
method.pitch: AnimationTree: base -> Add2(up, max(w,0)) -> Add2(down, max(-w,0)) -> Blend2 filtered to bone_sets.hands (amount 1, the aim grip); barrel = prop bone global basis * +Z; elev = asin(barrel.y); yaw = atan2(barrel.x, barrel.z); max_valid_* = largest |w| reached with strictly monotonic elevation and |yaw - yaw(0)| <= 8 deg (plan 5.4 rule, reference); max_monotonic_* = largest |w| with strictly monotonic elevation
method.pitch_range: solve_up / solve_down = max_monotonic_up / max_monotonic_down: the runtime inverts elev(w) over the authored additives' full monotonic range (the data limit). Today's player_anim.gd maps aim elevation onto the whole additive range (w in [-1, 1] at +-83 deg), and the owner's requirement keeps today's aim range, so the plan's yaw-drift limit (max_valid_*) does not cut it; the barrel yaw drift inside the range is in yaw_deg (solve_lateral_drift_deg = the largest sideways barrel deviation asin(sin(yaw - yaw(0)) * cos(elev)) inside it) for the AimStabilizer / per-pitch yaw correction (WP5). data_limits lists each side whose elevation at the end of the range stays inside +-60 deg (targets beyond it clamp)
method.pitch_skip: no pitch table and no chest height for the thrown-weapon profiles (actor_b_graph.json profiles.<w>.clip_set "throw"): the throw grip's prop bone is no barrel (tests/throwables/survey_throw_clips.gd; Throwable places the held object on the throw line itself), so UpperBody maps the aim elevation linearly onto the throw aim additives (UpperBody.PITCH_FALLBACK_DEG), and the chest mean stays the firearms' and the bow's
method.plant: normalized phase of each plant onset at 60 Hz: a foot is in contact when heel or ball is within 0.05 m of that point's lowest height and its ground speed |skeleton-space velocity (central difference) + body velocity| < max(0.30 m/s, 0.25 x body speed); body velocity = travel velocity for cyclic clips, and for one-shot clips -(velocity of the lowest point) median-filtered over +-0.10 s; contact runs closer than 0.10 s merge, runs shorter than 0.05 s drop; onset = first sample of a run (not at 0 for one-shot clips); cyclic clips wrap; l_contact / r_contact = [first, last contact sample] phase of every kept run (end > 1 when a cyclic run wraps the seam; a one-shot run from t = 0 included). Bank clips (cyclic) are the contract; one-shot onsets (starts, stops, landings) are best effort
method.travel: GA/vmm/bl/an.py method A: heel+ball at the clip's sample rate (key times); planted = within 0.02 m of the point's lowest height; least-squares slope per planted run of >= 3 samples (a cyclic clip's runs wrap the seam for points whose first/last samples meet within 0.02 m); body velocity = -(run-length-weighted mean foot velocity) (estimator method_a, quality native). Fallback chain when there is no such run (quality fallback): runs of >= 2 samples at the clip's own rate (method_a_run2), else runs of >= 3 at 2x then 4x the rate (method_a_2x / method_a_4x; travel.method_rate). kind: cyclic = the clip loops (see cyclic), speed / stride_m are its playback-rate reference; one_shot_mean = mean over the stance runs of a non-looping clip, not a rate reference (use body_profile)
method.travel_contact: secondary, informational: body velocity = -(mean skeleton-space velocity of heel/ball over every 60 Hz sample in contact as defined for plant), 6 passes starting from method A; steadier heading when method A has only 2-3-sample stances, speeds up to ~10 % off method A (it includes touchdown / toe-off)

units.space: skeleton space: forward +Z, left +X, up +Y; heading_deg and yaw_deg + = left

data_limits: down: the authored data reaches only -55.9 deg (w = -1.00, the full down additive); lower aim targets clamp there
